source_goal_version.digest_input_policy: relative_path+sha256+state+role over generated files and witness statements

problem_context.problem_statement: Verify a minimal read-only binary-search-tree traversal that follows left-child pointers from a valid non-null starting root to the end of the left spine.
problem_context.expected_behavior: Return a valid node reachable from the input root by zero or more left-child edges whose left child is None; preserve the abstract BST and all heap ownership.
problem_context.input_output_contract: Input is a nonempty valid BST rooted at root with tree_store(g). Output is a non-null valid node on the left spine with no left child, and tree_store(g) is unchanged.
spec_hint: Use the imported bst_lib_1 model, left_reachable, bst_left, bst_vvalid, bst_gvalid, and tree_store. Prefer a predicate-first left-spine invariant over a Rocq recursive mirror of the C loop.
preferred_hidden_properties: The current pointer remains valid and left-reachable from the original root; the full tree_store(g) is preserved.
forbidden_patterns: Do not define a Rocq recursive implementation of bst_leftmost or mirror the C loop as a state machine.
reference_case_hints: Use only QCP_demos_LLM BST/linked-structure examples and the supplied bst_lib_1 model; never inspect QCP_demos_human.

anti_patterns_avoided: No recursive Rocq implementation or loop-state machine.
No weakening of full tree ownership.

case_lib_spec_declarations.name: bst_leftmost_result
case_lib_spec_declarations.purpose: The result is a valid non-null node left-reachable from the original root and has no left child.

hidden_properties: The current pointer remains a valid non-null node.
The current node remains left-reachable from the original root.
The complete tree_store(g) resource and graph g remain unchanged.
